location: Malmstrom AFB RAPCON, Montana (author personal observation)
description: Author (16/17 yrs, janitor at Malmstrom tower) shown five unidentified radar 'targets' by FAA controller; two jets launched. Third-hand report from father: UFOs near Minuteman sites in Judith Basin ascended vertically at enormous speed.

location: Los Alamos, NM
description: Repeated sightings of 'unexplained phenomena' near AEC installation by OSI agents, airline & military pilots, security inspectors, citizens (FBI memo 1949-01-31). Another on 6 Jan 1949.

location: Los Alamos, NM
description: Dr. Lincoln La Paz sights green fireball crossing Los Alamos reservation; second fireball 8 days later seen by AEC security agent.

location: Oak Ridge, TN
description: No fewer than 14 separate UFO sightings reported by security officers, military pilots and radar personnel.

location: Hanford, WA / Moses Lake AFB
description: Silvery disc hovering over plant seen by Hanford personnel; tracked on radar at Moses Lake; F-82 scrambled; object left at high speed. Public Air Force explanation: conventional aircraft.

location: Hanford AEC plant, WA
description: Army Memo For Record (Maj. U.G. Carlan, from Lt Col Mildren): round objects above 15,000 ft; jet intercept attempts negative.

location: Richland WA (Hanford)
description: Four non-scheduled airline pilots (Baldwin, Robertson, Shenkel, Summers) reported saucer hovering near AEC plant (Miami Herald). Ruppelt later attributed to Skyhook balloon; Hastings doubts.

location: Hanford, WA
description: F-94 crew at 26,000 ft sees large round white object with dim reddish 'windows', radar lock-on, object reverses/dives; collision seemed imminent (Ruppelt).

location: Savannah River Plant, SC
description: Four DuPont employees saw four ~15-inch yellow/gold disks approaching '400 Area'; two more later; one rose to clear tanks (FBI letter Hoover to AFOSI/IG 1952-05-15).

location: Savannah River Plant, SC
description: John A. Anderson & ~100 engineers watched greenish object darting erratically ~2 min (McDonald 1968 House testimony; date uncertain).

location: Killeen Base / Camp Hood, TX
description: Flares/lights observed by guards: 6 & 8 Mar, 17 Mar (7 sightings, triangulated, Capt. Horace McCullough), 16 & 18 Apr; 27 Apr tiny ping-pong-ball lights within 6 ft of guards; 28 Apr 12 guards in 9 sightings. Army: objects 'bracketed' nuclear weapons area.

location: Camp Hood, TX
description: Conference of 4th Army, AFOSI, ONI, CIC, FBI, AFSWP: Army & Navy 'grave concern'; AFSWP: natural phenomena.

location: Sandia Base / Kirtland AFB, NM
description: Series: 6 Dec 1948 green fireball (Toulouse); 6 Jan 1949 diamond-shaped object at Ordnance Area (OSI SA Boling); 17 Feb 1949 fireball + cigar-shaped light seen by ~100 people (SA Neef); 13 Mar 1949; 27 Nov 1949 fireball (W.W. Jones, Lt Col Lancaster); 21 Mar 1950 multiple UFOs (10 OSI Spot Intel Reports); 24 Mar 1950 MPs saw objects.

location: Nevada Proving Ground (Yucca Flat), Buster-Jangle Charlie
description: Anonymous 'Mr. M.' (USAF airman from Nellis, sentry duty) reports 18 silvery domed discs in formation hovering 30-60 sec ~15-20 min before 14-kt Charlie shot; Sgt of the Guard said 'If we're smart, we won't say anything.' Walter Webb interviewed 1981 (phone), dated it by yield/sunrise.

location: Nevada test series Buster-Jangle Dog
description: Veteran Bernard Clark reports many unidentified airborne objects glinting at daybreak; Hastings judges likely sun glint off sampling/photo aircraft/B-50.

location: Over Albany, NY
description: F-86 pilots Capt. Howard F. Paulin and 2nd Lt. Lester F. Page report green flare descending at 26,000 ft, ~26 h after Ranger Baker-1 debris cloud passed Albany; Blue Book: inconclusive.

location: Near Abilene, TX (Airway G-5)
description: American Airlines DC-4 crew sees bright green projectile-shaped object pass at 4,500 ft and explode into red fireballs ~23 h after Buster Dog; debris cloud map shows Texas coverage (Keyhoe).

location: Arizona
description: Arizona Daily Star (3 Nov) 'Eerie Blue Flash Streaks Across Southwestern Skies', 9:05 pm MST, ~37 h after Dog.

location: Loring AFB, Maine (42nd Bomb Wing flight line)
description: 'John Smith' (42nd FMS jet mechanic) reports UFO hovering ~2-5 min over flight line as two Chrome Dome B-52s returned; large emergency turnout incl. many colonels; no aircraft damage; no discussion afterwards by witnesses (amnesia-like). Hastings dates it to Cuban Missile Crisis because tandem Chrome Dome sorties flew only then.

location: Echo Flight, Malmstrom AFB, MT (341st SMW)
description: All 10 Minuteman I missiles went No-Go ~0830 due to guidance & control faults; UFOs reportedly seen by maintenance teams at two widely separated LFs and confirmed by Security Alert Team before dawn. Official wing history: UFO rumors 'disproven'. Boeing investigators duplicated faults by injecting 'noise' into logic coupler; source unknown.

location: Oscar Flight (LCF Oscar), Malmstrom AFB, MT
description: Salas/Meiwald: guards report glowing red saucer hovering at LCF front gate; guard injured approaching; then 6-8 missiles go No-Go at once, mostly G&C. OSI debrief, NDAs signed, alert logs confiscated. Air Force records do not acknowledge the incident.

location: Kilo Flight LCF, Malmstrom AFB
description: Airman James Ortyl and A2C Robert Pounders saw shimmering reddish-orange object pass within ~30 yds of dispatch office window; unreported.

location: US Route 87 near Belt, MT
description: Trucker Ken Williams reports dome-shaped bright object landing in ravine; Cascade County deputies notified Malmstrom; Great Falls Tribune coverage; declassified AF telex confirms notification.

location: Malmstrom missile silo (unnamed)
description: Round white object circled a missile silo for prolonged periods; personnel told it was secret test vehicle (Fowler, from civilian employee).

location: Malmstrom AFB flight line
description: SSgt Louis D. Kenneweg (341st MIMS) saw zigzagging light looming over flight line while driving to work.

date_text: 1964-09 (candidate dates 2, 3, 15 Sept per Jacobs log; Hastings favors 15 Sept 1964)
location: Big Sur, CA telescope site / Vandenberg AFB (Atlas D RV test) / Pacific
description: Lt. Bob Jacobs (1369th Photo Sqn, OIC Photo Instrumentation) says Image Orthicon telescope film of Atlas ICBM re-entry vehicle test showed domed disc UFO circle the dummy warhead, emit four flashes, warhead tumbled and fell hundreds of miles short of Eniwetok; film shown once or thrice at Vandenberg, then confiscated by 'agents'.

location: Harlowton / K-1 LCF, Malmstrom, MT
description: Harlowton Times (20 Feb 1975): 3 deputies see 3 UFOs; 0200 Air Policemen at K-1 report object hovering over K-10, 7 mi N of Harlowton airport.

location: Malmstrom AFB ICBM field (M-1, L-1, L-3, L-5, L-6, K-1, K-4, LIMA, Harlowton LCF), MT
description: 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's log: SAT/LCF crews report red/orange/yellow objects, objects 'issuing a black tubular object', height radar picks up 2-7 objects at 10-13,000 ft, J330 stationary then 7 kt at 12,000 ft; two F-106s scrambled from Great Falls; lights extinguish when fighters approach and return when they leave; 9 Nov 'orange white disc object'.

location: Minot AFS, ND
description: Bright star-like object passed over radar station at 1,000-2,000 ft, no noise (NORAD log 1125Z).

location: Loring AFB WSA, ME
description: Documented incursion at Weapons Storage Area (per author; documents in Ch 18-onward).

location: Freezeout Lake, ~40 mi WNW of Malmstrom (B-52 practice runs)
description: Montana Fish & Game employee saw small round white light behind B-52, appearing to attach to it; bomber radar reportedly malfunctioned (Cascade Co. Sheriff Capt. Keith Wolverton; AF denied knowledge).

location: Malmstrom missile field / Loring WSA (SAC HQ daily recap)
description: Col. John W. Haley III recalls SAC daily report describing UFO hovering over Loring WSA (thought to be taking radiation readings) and UFO following a Malmstrom missile crew; F-106 intercepts from Minot (Hastings: no documentation of Minot launches; Great Falls fighters used).

location: Titan II complex 570-1, near Oracle AZ (570th SMS, Davis-Monthan AFB)
description: APRO (Lorenzens, 1969): brilliant light descending over site at midnight; two jets scrambled; object left north, returned minutes later; 3 anonymous witnesses. Hastings notes site was not yet operational on that date (no missile until 8 Dec 1962), so witnesses likely contractors.

location: F.E. Warren AFB, WY (90th SMW): LCFs Echo, Golf, Quebec; LFs B-4, E-2, G-1, H-2
description: Blue Book OOD Lt. Anspaugh logged calls from base commander (Col. Johnson), command post (Capt. Snelling), Sioux Army Depot CO etc. reporting circular colored silent object; explained by Air Force as twinkling stars (per Ch.16 ref at line 13056).

location: RAF Woodbridge / Rendlesham Forest / RAF Bentwaters, Suffolk, UK
description: Halt memo 'Unexplained Lights' (13 Jan 1981): triangular object in forest; depressions 1.5 in deep, 7 in dia; radiation 0.1 mR; star-like objects; beams of light. Hastings: dates in memo misstated; actual 26 Dec ~0300 and night of 27/28 Dec.

location: RAF Bentwaters Weapons Storage Area
description: Unidentified security personnel reported luminous object hovering above WSA that sent laser-like beams down near/onto bunkers; Halt only heard radio chatter (he was in the forest) and saw beams elsewhere on base.

location: Vandenberg AFB area, CA
description: Civilian UFO sightings in local newspapers within days of first Atlas-Ds going on alert (book ref 1).

location: Walker AFB, NM - 579th SMS Atlas Site 9 (west of Roswell)
description: Repeated (3-10) occasions of silent objects hovering over silo and shining lights; guards frightened (Nelson DMCCC from launch capsule, did not see). Goss (guard) saw erratic fast lights twice, 2-3 weeks apart, winter 1963-64; told by launch commander they were military aircraft (once per SAC HQ duty officer).

location: Walker AFB Atlas Site 9 perimeter fence
description: Missile facilities technician Bob Caplan and guard approached ~6-inch flat circular yellowish light on ground outside fence; vanished when flashlights shone on it, reappeared 20-30 ft away. Caplan later interviewed by Walker AFOSI.

location: Walker AFB (on base)
description: Fast-moving, erratic star-like light seen by many; Caplan later told by 6th Combat Defense Sq member it was tracked on radar and jets chased (hearsay; fighters presumably from Holloman). Kaminski: ~half his barracks watched 2-5 star-like lights for ~15 min doing 90-degree turns, no sonic booms.

location: Atlas site NE of Walker AFB
description: A1C Tom Kaminski (topside): two 'star' lights moving in unison; base told capsule radar had them and fighters were sent; next morning debrief: 'What UFOs? We didn't send up any fighters.'

location: Walker AFB Atlas Sites 6, 7, 8 (SSE of Roswell)
description: Lt Philip Moore (DMCCC at Site 7): crew at Sites 6/8 reported UFO hovering and rapidly shuttling; Site 7 crew (TSgt Jack Nevins, A1C Garner, A1C Rundag, Maj Dan Gilbert) saw silent light. Nevins: 'I cannot say I saw a UFO, only a light in the sky'; night crystal clear. No equipment effects; no debrief.

location: Walker AFB Atlas Site 8 (Route 285 south of Roswell) and other sites
description: A2C Barry Krause's letter to NICAP: frequent sightings, guards afraid; EPT saw weird light, capsule commander called SAC CP; SAC said KC-135 in area; object shot out of sight after tanker flew over; a Lt Col allegedly told to keep quiet; incident reports 'top secret'.

location: F.E. Warren AFB Atlas Site 1 (564th SMS)
description: MSgt Harold Renninger (then SSgt) and perimeter guard saw extremely bright silent light above dirt landing strip for 2-3 min; guard said Helio Courier; Renninger doubts. Other later lights near site (helicopters? spotlights?).

location: F.E. Warren AFB Site 1 Pad 1 (566th SMS area)
description: A1C Arthur McEnaney and guards saw round bright object hovering ~midnight; interceptors from Denver reportedly said weather balloon; told to keep quiet by SSgt Fred Coffer (national security).

location: FAA/Air Force SAGE building, Malmstrom AFB
description: Grover Austad (FAA controller, SAGE bldg): object tracked ~2,400 mph, zigzagged hundreds of miles; ADC controller confirmed seeing it; logged by FAA and reported to ADC (no feedback).

location: Salt Lake ATC Center / Burley, Idaho / Hill AFB
description: Austad: caller reports huge cigar-shaped object 60-70 mi N of Burley; F-80 from Hill AFB scrambled; pilot reportedly said 21 disc-shaped craft came out; object ~80,000 ft above pilot's ceiling.

location: National Reactor Testing Station, Idaho
description: Keyhoe (Flying Saucer Conspiracy): blinding glow over AEC test station at 12:40 am; witnesses Kelly Brooks and A.L. Taylor; Idaho Falls Post Register and AP reported; several earlier 'flash-bulb' lights.

location: Malmstrom RAPCON, Great Falls MT
description: Paul Selley: five unknown targets crossed scope very fast (no hover, no scramble recalled); several tracking events at night 7-11 pm; objects 'thousands of mph'. Hastings determines this was not the March 1967 event he saw (those five were stationary and fighters launched).

location: Malmstrom RAPCON / SAGE
description: O.P. 'Pote' Morrow (RAPCON supervisor 1967-80) recalls fighters vectored southwest to unknown targets, nothing found; Kittleson: unknowns tracked near Lewistown and closer to Great Falls, aircraft scrambled from Great Falls; Weinzetl: ~1,700 mph high-altitude target ~20 s with Jerry Webster.

location: Minot AFB, Echo LCC (91st SMW), flights Alpha through Oscar
description: Lt David H. Schuur (DMCCC, Echo capsule) says a single bright object moved flight by flight (Alpha->Oscar, SE to NW) reported over PAS; Echo capsule received spurious indications incl. 'Launch in Progress' on several missiles, forced use of Inhibit switch; reset in minutes; logs/tapes collected, 'nothing happened' order; no OSI debrief.

location: F.E. Warren AFB, India Flight LCC area
description: Capt Larry Johnson (MCCC): light low to ground silently moved from LCC to LCC; SAT chased 10-15 min but could not close; not helicopter/airplane; no missile effects; no OSI debrief.

location: Minot AFB, ND: LFs O-6, N-7, Oscar/November LCFs, Bowbells area; B-52 inbound (5th BW)
description: Camper/maintenance teams and Base Ops log report bright maneuvering object near N-7; weather radar tracks object near Bowbells; B-52 radar paced by return 'as big or bigger than a KC-135' for ~20 mi, UHF transmitters disrupted; radarscope camera 14 frames; B-52 directed over ground-hovering oval orange object with tube and crescent; Blue Book case 12,548.

location: Minot AFB missile field
description: Larry Manross (launch crew commander 1966-70 per post) says UFOs were so frequent guards put chairs in front of LCFs to watch; one night an object 'buzzed' the LCF; radar tracked it; no report requested.

location: Minot AFB missile field, ND
description: Hynek (SEP, Dec 1966) summarized a preliminary AF report: launch control radio disrupted by static; guards saw a UFO that appeared to land; strike-team radio also disrupted ~10 miles from landing site; object rose and passed beneath a second identical object; Minot radar tracked both. Fowler later told the Christian Science Monitor (5 Dec 1973); the Air Force said SAC unit histories showed nothing.

location: Malmstrom AFB, LF M-6 ("Kilo Triangle"), MT
description: Hearsay via anonymous retired SP: Camper Alert Team at M-6 illuminated by bright light from the sky; site possibly went off alert; guard allegedly took Polaroids; reported to command post; not publicised.

location: F.E. Warren AFB, India LCC/LF (90th SMW)
description: Billings (Golf LCC deputy) overheard on all-LCC UHF net: India LCC Outer then Inner Security Zone alarms at an LF; SAT saw large bright UFO (rotating colored lights around orange glow) hover ~1 min, move off, speed away; 19 other LCCs heard; crews warned to be silent; rumor OSI came by helicopter and that 'target tapes' on three warheads were erased (maintenance rumor).

location: F.E. Warren AFB, Kilo LCC area silo
description: Second-hand (via a maintenance 1Lt, ~3 days later): entire maintenance crew watched a UFO maneuver near a Minuteman III silo for ~5 minutes.

location: F.E. Warren AFB, Charlie LCC
description: SAT staff sergeant and two SPs told Billings a UFO landed near the LCC overnight with a minute-by-minute report to the capsule; the sergeant allegedly got into trouble and OSI was involved.

location: Fischbach Army Depot (Area 3 special-weapons storage), Germany
description: PFC R. Jack Phillips (193rd MP Bn) alone in Tower 4 after waking from 'deep observation' saw a bright 'star' in the north approach fast, hover ~100 yds beyond the fence as a ~60-ft domed disc with green glow; security lights, field phone and generators failed ~30 s, then all bunker alarms sounded; no debrief; no other witnesses known.

location: Grand Forks AFB bomber alert area, ND
description: Report to Hynek from an anonymous USAF officer: within 3 minutes 14 SP sentries, 2 pilots and a B-52 maintenance supervisor reported two large dark oval objects with five small lights each hovering ~1,500 ft for 2 min then drifting south with a faint hum; SP radio interference; tower radar off-line; no scheduled aircraft within 150 mi; patrol found no ground traces; WSA dogs nervous.

location: Safeguard ABM complex (Nekoma/Stanley R. Mickelson), ND
description: Anonymous ex-Army sergeants recall: officers discussing very fast objects over Canadian airspace (4th-5th time), fighters arrived after they vanished; an MP recalls a soldier seeing lights over the missile field who was not taken seriously; others recall nothing.

location: Airborne Launch Control System aircraft, ~50 mi east of Ellsworth AFB, SD
description: Lt Col Frank Hale, in the jumpseat on final approach, saw a silver globe pacing the aircraft, stopping, climbing, and maneuvering at high speed for 2-3 minutes; pilots/navigator apparently did not see it; no radar/radio effects; unreported (Human Reliability Program).

location: McConnell AFB Titan II complexes, KS (381st SMW)
description: Manson (MFT) and Dziewulski (crew commander) relay SP-team reports of a stationary airborne vehicle over complex 533-5 (1976-79) leaving quickly and 'UFO incident' stories from a former commander; neither saw anything.

location: Logan County CO (inside F.E. Warren missile field)
description: 'Big Mama and the baby UFOs' — bright stationary light dropping small lights; Sheriff Tex Graves links lights to 77 (later 74) cattle mutilations in the county (MUFON Journal, Bob Pratt); CBI/CSU later attributed most to predators.

location: Foxtrot Flight, Ellsworth AFB (near Mud Butte), SD
description: Patterson ranch family: mutilated cattle on their property, lights near LF F-09, disc-shaped UFO at dusk, strike-team leader borrowed binoculars saying radar had an object over the LF.

location: Las Animas County, CO
description: Sheriff Lou Girodo and a deputy saw an orange 'moon' rising near a mutilated cow site split into two bright orange objects; one raced away horizontally, the other descended behind a hill.

location: Delta-3 LF, Ellsworth AFB (Delta Flight, near Wall SD)
description: TSgt John W. Mills III (then A1C, combat targeting team) and 2Lt team chief, with a topside guard, report a loud low-frequency hum felt through the body, a black region overhead with a straight edge and ~60-70 deg corners (rhombus), no stars inside it; site lights, truck and radio died, G&C No-Go; object gone when power returned; command post/job control angry; teams told to say nothing; two other teams (Echo, third unnamed) reported similar; hearsay that ~12-13 missiles (all Echo, part of Delta incl. D-1) went down.

location: Ellsworth AFB flight line / B-52 alert pad, SD
description: Mills and 3-4 others on a barracks roof (waiting for an SR-71 takeoff) saw a dark triangular object ~0.5 mi away, visible to the naked eye but invisible through binoculars, ~500 ft, moving along the runway, then vanishing; Mills says a Flash message the same day barred discussion and a second Flash next day said the event did not happen.

location: F.E. Warren AFB, WY (WSA, base patrol)
description: Jay DeSisto (A1C, 90th SPG law-enforcement desk sergeant) recalls repeated WSA reports of 'lights' overhead (outcomes unremembered) and, three times, off-duty recall to arm and guard the base because of 'satellites' allegedly overhead; clusters of 2-3 nights; he never heard of UFOs. Hastings suggests a UFO link.

location: Kirtland AFB, Manzano WSA / Coyote Canyon, NM
description: AFOSI complaint form (quoted): 3 security policemen saw a very bright light stop over Coyote Canyon, 'land', later rise vertically; ~30 min later a Sandia guard saw a disk-shaped object near an alarmed structure, his radio failed, object left vertically. Hastings defers to Maccabee's 1980s investigation.

location: Byelokoroviche (Belokorovichi), Ukrainian SSR (missile base)
description: ABC Prime Time Live 1994: ex-Soviet officers (Plantonev/'Plutinov', Chernovshev) describe hours-long disc over a base, missiles' launch-prep lights coming on and a 15-second countdown aborted. History Channel 2004 (Platov): flare drop by a nearby unit.

location: Katta-Kurgan tactical missile base, Uzbek SSR
description: Per Ted R. Phillips (MUFON 2005) citing Dr S.P. Kuzionov: five witnesses incl. technician Shamil Yuaihmetov saw a cigar-shaped metallic object descend slowly at 45 deg, hissing; next day three landing marks in a triangle in a vineyard (0.5 m deep).

location: Kapustin Yar (missile test range/depot), Russia
description: From a KGB file via Don Berliner: 7 military witnesses saw up to three objects; a 4-5 m disc with beam hovered 20-70 m over the warhead depot for ~2 hours; fighter scrambled could not approach. Hastings compares to Bentwaters.

location: Alpha Flight LF A-03 near Monarch, MT (Malmstrom)
description: SSgt Joseph Brown and a partner (camper team, site topside security down) watch a bright light making sudden direction changes for ~2 h; LF A-10 team ~10 mi away also sees it; FSC overhears; light 'goes straight up', fuzzy triangle outline at dawn; maintenance/SET arrive 0730 asking about it; captain invokes PRP.

location: Roads near Monarch/Belt and Malmstrom flight line, MT
description: TSgt Mills sees a bright light 'helicopter' making a 90-degree banked turn; road block near Belt; unofficially hears of 'anomalies' at missile sites and balls of light over the flight line (softball-sized one flew into a vehicle barn), two tankers diverted to Hill and Minot; no missiles went off alert.

location: India Flight LF I-04, Malmstrom (Goodrich MUFON report)
description: Alert Response Team and a maintenance team (via technician to Goodrich) see a slow, low, large light with multi-colored smaller lights; minutes later maintenance team sees a very bright green fireball. Hastings accepts Webb's meteor explanation for the fireball only.

location: Great Falls MT (seen from Missile Roll Transfer Bldg, Malmstrom)
description: TSgt Goodrich and a lieutenant see five bright white isosceles-triangle objects at ~75 deg elevation moving slowly N to S, pausing twice 10-15 s, then speeding SW; clear, -15 F; towers report nothing (neither tracks above 10,000 ft).

location: Ellsworth AFB, SD (44th FMMS hangar)
description: A1C Reager and A1C Berrier see a rigid formation of bright white lights move rapidly toward the maintenance hangar, hover briefly and vanish behind low cloud (5-10 s); MUFON forms by Goodrich within two days.

location: F.E. Warren AFB, WY (Bravo-02 and other LFs)
description: 'John Blake' (319th MS launch officer) reports guards spooked at an LF and told a friend a formation of lights 'buzzed' them at B-02, sworn to secrecy; a nearby cattle mutilation; none first-hand to Blake.

location: F.E. Warren AFB, WY (chow hall)
description: NUFORC report: star-like object zipped around the sky for 30 s with no sound (posted 2003).

location: Romeo LCF, F.E. Warren AFB (Chugwater, WY)
description: NUFORC report: bright light moved slowly ~20 s then flew off fast leaving a white tail; coworkers say many have seen it (posted 2003).

location: Jemez Mountains NM (near Los Alamos) and Santa Fe NM
description: A friend of Hastings' camping family sees a 'satellite' turn sharply and then a large light with five small lights merging and two leaving; Patrick Ortiz of Santa Fe videotapes a white disc changing color and hovering for 3+ h from ~0300 (Santa Fe New Mexican, 23 Jul 1996).

location: Near Los Alamos NM
description: Patricia Hoyt (posted online) sees a white light zigzag, rise, expand 500x, and a disk-shaped object; the rental car would not start until it left.

location: Los Lunas NM (near Kirtland AFB complex)
description: Hastings acquaintance 'Gene' sees a bright white light retreat from Albuquerque as an F-15/F-16 chases it and the light outruns the jet; Gene also saw a hovering luminous object at INEL in 1967.

location: Savannah River Plant, SC (New Ellenton)
description: NUFORC report (posted 2003) of a wingless oblong low-flying silent object 'sliding' from west to north heading.

location: Nevada-Arizona (Phoenix)
description: Phoenix Lights: reports of a huge wedge/V-shaped object with lights from Henderson NV to Tucson ~1855-2030, and a string of flares-like lights ~2200 south of Phoenix; Luke AFB later attributes the latter to flares dropped by A-10s from the Goldwater range. Hastings says it has no nuclear link.

location: Conrad, Pondera County, MT (near Papa LCF and LFs S-40 and Q-15)
description: Ryan Riewer: on 7 Dec ~2230 a very fast light from the SW stops, turns 90 deg, 'lands' ~0.5-1 mi away near a missile silo; on 11 Dec several stationary lights with blue, red and white lights for ~30 min; plus mutilated cows (Oct-Nov 2006) and an AP story of an apparently 'dropped' cow near Valier.

location: Placitas, NM (author's home)
description: Hastings sees a red light on a NNE track suddenly expand 20-30x for ~5 s and shrink, silently.
